name: Fray
author: E. T. Carter
description: Combed, then released. Diagonal fibres run sleek and parallel where a comb has just passed and fray into domain-warped chaos in the length they have not yet reached. A bright comb stroke sweeps along the fibres over and over, re-ordering the weave behind it and leaving it to unravel ahead, so the whole field breathes order into chaos and back. Two parallax depth layers fray at different rates.

params.label: Thread count
params.effect: Density of fibres across the weave; low gives a few broad ribbons, high a fine combed hair.

params.label: Fray
params.effect: How violently the released length unravels; 0 keeps the whole field combed and sleek, high tangles the tips into wild chaos.

params.label: Comb speed
params.effect: Speed the comb stroke sweeps along the fibres; 0 holds a fixed order-to-chaos gradient, high re-combs the weave in rapid passes.

params.label: Strokes
params.effect: How many comb strokes span the frame at once; low is one long sweep root to tip, high stacks several order-and-fray bands.

params.label: Glow
params.effect: Overall emission of the fibres; low is a quiet weave, high a luminous combed sheet.

params.label: Hue spread
params.effect: How far the palette shifts from the combed end to the frayed end; 0 holds one hue, high colours order and chaos distinctly.

params.label: Depth
params.effect: Parallax separation between the near and far fibre layers and how much the far one dims; low flattens them, high sinks the far weave back.
